Headline: TrustedVolumes Recovers $2M in ETH After Hacker Settlement 🚨

What happened
- TrustedVolumes has recovered $2 million in ETH following a direct settlement with the attacker who stole $5.87 million in May 2026.
- About half of the stolen funds have been returned through negotiations, not litigation.

Why it matters
- A rare case where a portion of stolen crypto was voluntarily returned by the perpetrator.
- Signals that on-chain tracking and pressure can sometimes yield results beyond traditional legal channels.
- Keeps community confidence intact while highlighting ongoing risks in DeFi infrastructure.

Key takeaways
- Recovery progress: ~$2M back out of $5.87M stolen (roughly 34% recovered).
- Method: Direct negotiation leading to voluntary return rather than court order or exchange freeze.
- Impact: Partial relief for affected users and creditors; operational costs may still loom.

Market context
- Bitcoin remains well above $100,000 amid broader altcoin momentum.
- On-chain analytics continue to play an increasingly important role in tracing illicit flows.

Risk reminder
- Even with partial recoveries, exposure remains high; always prioritize security audits and cold storage best practices.

- CPA Australia publicly references Ripple/XRP in its communications, highlighting growing institutional attention to digital assets. 🏛️
